title: A morphism of sheaves of sets is an epimorphism iff it is surjective on all stalks
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ a morphism of sheaves of sets on $X$ (sheaves on the site of open subsets of $X$ with open coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]). For a presheaf of sets $\mathcal P$ on $X$ and $x\in X$ let $\mathcal P_x=\varinjlim_{U\ni x}\mathcal P(U)$ be its stalk, the colimit of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] over the open neighbourhoods $U$ of $x$ ordered by reverse inclusion, with germs $s\mapsto s_x$, and let $\varphi_x:\mathcal F_x\to\mathcal G_x$ be the unique map with $\varphi_x(s_x)=(\varphi_U(s))_x$ for every open $U\ni x$ and $s\in\mathcal F(U)$. Then $\varphi$ is an epimorphism in the category of sheaves of sets on $X$ (for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal H$ and morphisms $g,h:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ with $g\circ\varphi=h\circ\varphi$ one has $g=h$) if and only if $\varphi_x$ is surjective for every $x\in X$.
